glossary.definition: The user's preference, stored as a JSON attribute on their directory user: allowedActions (action tiers), maxAmount (spend cap), detectAgent, unknownAgentPolicy (allow / hitl / deny for a detected AI agent).
A blocked-but-approvable agent action is answered HTTP 428 with a task id; a human approves or denies. An approval is a single-use receipt: the retried call passes once.

PingOne Protect's bot detection names the AI agent type (rules 660-674, e.g. "AI agent - Muse detected") when the Signals SDK runs with agent identification. In AI-DEMO2 it is a session-start signal; per-call evaluation is an open question.

sources.title: RFC 8693: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
sources.use: Defines the act (actor) claim that marks a call as agent-originated.

cards.label: Scenario 1: Permitted: read tool, read allowed
cards.description: The tier is in the allowed list, no cap applies to reads, and nothing detected an agent: permit.

cards.label: Scenario 2: HITL: write tool, user allows read only
cards.description: The tool needs the write tier; the user only allowed read. The call is not lost — it becomes a human-approval task (HTTP 428).

cards.label: Scenario 3: HITL: amount over the spend cap
cards.description: The tier is allowed but the amount (750) exceeds the 500 cap. The cap reason is what the human sees.

cards.label: Scenario 4: HITL: Protect detects an AI agent
cards.description: Mock Protect named an AI agent at session start and the default policy is hitl: even an allowed read goes to a human first.

cards.label: Scenario 5: Denied: Protect detection with a deny policy
cards.description: The user chose to deny detected agents outright: HTTP 403, no approval path. The strictest preference wins.

cards.label: Set your own preferences
cards.description: Edit allowed tiers, the spend cap and the unknown-agent policy; the gate answers on the next tool call.

cards.label: Doctor and health
cards.description: Preflight checks and the demo-health/1 endpoint.
